summary: Nate B. Jones, an AI strategy commentator, discusses a market for work archives (Slack, Teams, email) sold to train AI agents, centered on Google's $10M winning bid for bankrupt Spirit Airlines' records. He argues these records capture the performance of work rather than the work itself, so agents trained on them will mimic work without understanding it. He also covers Mercor's training environments, data brokers, worker and union pushback, and what he sees as useful agent design (structured data for agents). The talk is about agent training data and workplace impact, not about interfaces.
speakers_or_authors: Nate B. Jones (AI News & Strategy Daily)
relevance_reason: Touches the computer-use agent theme only indirectly. It is about how labs source training data for knowledge-work agents and whether agents can do the work, not about interface or product changes. Contains some opinion on agent usefulness but no hands-on tests or shipped products.

claims.claim: Google made the winning $10M bid for Spirit Airlines' work records in the August auction, beating Mercor's $7.5M bid; a hearing on the sale is set for Oct 14.
claims.quote: In the August auction, Google made the winning $10 million bid over Mercor that beds seven and a half.

claims.claim: Mercor announced plans to acquire DeepTune, which builds training environments where agents attempt assignments and are checked for success, and pays experts to define success checks.
claims.quote: Mercor announced plans in July to acquire DeepTune, which builds training environments.

claims.claim: Spirit's inventory listed about 100 million emails and half a billion Teams records.
claims.quote: Their August inventory listed 100 million emails and believe it or not, a half a billion teams records

claims.claim: Work archives capture the performance of work as much as the work, so agents trained on them may learn the wrong lessons, such as treating a closed ticket as success.
claims.quote: How does the agent learn anything except the performance of work?

claims.claim: Data for sale is disproportionately from failing companies, since sellers are those with no other use for it.
claims.quote: disproportionately likely to be from failing companies

claims.claim: Spirit's flight attendant union raised concerns about confidential employee information in the records.
claims.quote: The spirit flight attendant union raised concerns about confidential employee information

claims.claim: Some leaders privately estimate that up to a third of their teams quietly resist AI tools.
claims.quote: leaders who estimate as many as a third of their teams are passively, quietly sabotaging and resisting these AI tools

claims.claim: Agents trained on Slack/Teams traces will imitate work, producing a costly simulation, e.g. empty stand-up messages.
claims.quote: a bunch of agents who are very good at sending stand-up messages that say nothing to report here

claims.claim: Agent value lies in repeatable drudgery work run through systems without human conversational channels, not in imitating human workflows.
claims.quote: the agent reading the data, the agent processing the data, and the agent outputting a particular format

claims.claim: Claude-made PowerPoints are recognizable and solve layout but not thinking or alignment; AI output isn't real work unless the user understands it.
claims.quote: you can tell a cloud PowerPoint from a mile away

claims.claim: The best agent-collaboration work he has seen is structuring data (e.g. markdown files) so agents and humans can use it, in product and engineering teams.
claims.quote: people invest a ton in good markdown files that agents can read and that humans can use to query

commercial_interest: No sponsorship disclosed. Jones is a commentator who sells AI strategy and consulting content and says he advises leaders; he mentions Glean and Mercor critically with no stated stake.
older_event: The Spirit Airlines auction occurred in August (more than 30 days before publication) but the sale hearing is still pending for Oct 14; the new element is the commentary framing. Not primarily about an interface event.
